OAuth2 Client token placement broken for URI_QUERY and BODY

#### Description

When using OAuth2 Client with token placement set to `URI_QUERY` or `BODY`, the bearer token is being added to the wrong location. The token that should be added to the URI query parameters is instead being added to the request body, and the token that should be added to the request body is instead being added to the headers.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```python
from oauthlib.oauth2 import Client
from oauthlib.oauth2.rfc6749 import URI_QUERY, BODY

# Create client with access token
client = Client('client_id', access_token='test_token')

# Test URI_QUERY placement - token should be added to URI
uri, headers, body = client.add_token(
    'https://example.com/api', 
    body='original_body', 
    headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'}, 
    token_placement=URI_QUERY
)
print("URI:", uri)  # Expected: https://example.com/api?access_token=test_token
print("Body:", body)  # Expected: original_body

# Test BODY placement - token should be added to body
uri, headers, body = client.add_token(
    'https://example.com/api', 
    body='original_body', 
    headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'}, 
    token_placement=BODY
)
print("URI:", uri)  # Expected: https://example.com/api
print("Headers:", headers)  # Expected: {'Content-Type': 'application/json'}
```

The token placement is completely mixed up - URI_QUERY placement puts the token in the body instead of the URI, and BODY placement puts the token in headers instead of the body.
</issue>
